newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar leaps to new highs, stocks surge in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar leaps to new highs, stocks surge in Tokyo.

text.p: The resurgent dollar strode to its highest level in nearly four years against the Japanese yen on Wednesday, although the long-suffering Tokyo stock market got a break with a sharp rise in prices.
Traders said the yen was hit by lingering concerns about Japan's banking sector.
But the stock market was more upbeat, with the key Nikkei index soaring 3.78 percent to close 655.72 points higher at 18,013.88.
Traders said the climb above the psychologically important 18,000-point level came after reports that the government may scrap taxes on securities transactions.
In a newspaper report, a senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official was quoted as saying the ministry would likely reach a conclusion on how to revamp the tax by June.

"We had been dubious about whether the government was going to take steps to support the stock market, but it looks as if they are finally trying to take action," said a trader at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
The tax is seen as a major dampener on the Tokyo share market. Similar taxes have been scrapped in other major trading centres in order to help spur growth in the markets.
Brokers have been looking for action from the government to halt the market's recent downward spiral of nearly 14 percent since early December.
Brokers said futures contracts in sectors such as banking were being bought back after heavy selling in past weeks. Blue-chip shares were also being sought by foreign investors.

On the currency market, the dollar rose to 118.75 yen, a 46-month high, in Tokyo trading on a round of buying by interbank traders and renewed worries about the health of Japanese banks. This compared with a level of around 117.91 yen in late U.S. trade on Tuesday.
In the early afternoon, apparently unfounded rumours circulated that some regional banks were in deeper financial difficulties, prompting a round of yen sales for the U.S. currency, dealers said.

Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita showed his displeasure with the surging dollar, saying that the pace of recent movements in the currency market has been rather sharp and the central bank will continue to watch their effect on the economy.

The surging U.S. currency also hit a fresh 31-month high of 1.6345 marks on a newspaper report that Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said the dollar's strength was in line with the wishes of the powerful Group of Seven nations.
Japanese government bond prices rose as some big investors said they would remain in the safe-haven of government debt instead of risking their money on the uncertain stock market.
"Nobody believes the stock market's downtrend is over," said one senior dealer at a major securities house.
